neighbours.label: the measure word of a quantity phrase: 'half the', 'a few', 'number of', '<n> <units> of', counted units like 'two drinks' / 'three days'; 'of' in non-quantity uses stays quiet
fire: The team lost half the matches it played away from home.
The bread needs only a few minutes in a hot oven.
The machine repeats the cycle a fixed number of times.
The trench cut through 6 ft. of sand above the bedrock.
She spent half the afternoon looking for her keys.
The paint dries after just a few hours in the sun.
A large number of seats were still empty at noon.
Guests who had three or more drinks were offered a taxi.
quiet: The team lost its captain to injury away from home.
The bread is the pride of the bakery on the corner.
The machine is the work of a retired engineer.
The trench exposed the wall of an old cellar.
She is the daughter of a teacher and a nurse.
The paint has the colour of wet slate.
The mayor of the town spoke at noon.
Guests praised the taste of the soup and the bread.

notes: Card: ' of' after '3 ft.' and 'number', ' half', ' few', ' days', ' drinks'. Probes: half 0.62, few 0.64, number of 0.43, drinks 0.40, '3 ft. of' 0.34, 'three days' 0.20; 'author of the book' 0.02, 'capital of France' 0.03. The - pole is psychology/professor-of.
